questions.q: Choose the correct stability order of the given free radicals.
questions.solution:
In compounds (I), (III) and (IV) the -M effect and hyperconjugation effect are inoperative at meta positions. So we should consider the inductive effect of the groups. -I effect will decrease the stability of the free radical by withdrawing the electrons toward it itself. The order of -I effect is \(\mathrm{NO}_2 \gt \mathrm{CN} \gt \mathrm{OH}\). Therefore (III) is most destabilised.
In compound (II) the OH act as electron donating group through +M effect which is operative at para position. This increase the electron density at para position and stabilise the free radical. Hence compound (1) is most stabilised. The order of stability of free radical is
\(\text { II } \gt \text { I } \gt \text { IV } \gt \text { III }\)

$\mathrm{P}\left(\frac{\mathrm{B}}{\mathrm{A}}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B} \cap \mathrm{A})}{\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A})}=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B} \cap \mathrm{A})=\frac{1}{8}\mathrm{P}\left(\frac{\mathrm{A}}{\mathrm{B}}\right)=\frac{1}{4} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A} \cap \mathrm{B})}{\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B})}=\frac{1}{4} \Rightarrow \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B})=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A} \cap \mathrm{B})=\frac{1}{8}=\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A}) \cdot \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B})\therefore$ Events A and B are independent.
Now, $\mathrm{P}\left(\frac{\mathrm{A}^{\prime}}{\mathrm{B}}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A} \cap \mathrm{B})}{\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B})}=\frac{\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A}) \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B})}{\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B})}=\frac{3}{4}$

to $n$ terms
$=\tan ^{-1}\left\{\frac{1}{1+x(x+1)}\right\}+\tan ^{-1}\left\{\frac{1}{1+(x+1)(x+2)}\right\}+\tan ^{-1}\left\{\frac{1}{1+(x+2)(x+3)}\right\}+\ldots \ldots \ldots+\tan ^{-1}\left\{\frac{1}{1+(x+(n-1))(x+n)}\right\}=\tan ^{-1}\left\{\frac{(x+1)-x}{1+(x+1) x}\right\}+\tan ^{-1}\left\{\frac{(x+2)-(x+1)}{1+(x+2)(x+1)}\right\}+\tan ^{-1}\left\{\frac{(x+3)-(x+2)}{1+(x+3)(x+2)}\right\}+\ldots .+\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{(x+n)-(x+n-1)}{1+(x+n)(x+n-1)}\right)\therefore y=\left\{\tan ^{-1}(x+1)-\tan ^{-1}(x)\right\}+\left\{\tan ^{-1}(x+2)-\tan ^{-1}(x+1)\right\}+\left\{\tan ^{-1}(x+3)-\tan ^{-1}(x+2)\right\}+\ldots \ldots . .+\left\{\tan ^{-1}(x+n)-\tan ^{-1}[x+(n-1)]\right\}$

questions.q: The variance of 20 observations is 5 . If each observation is multiplied by 2 , then the new variance of the resulting observation is
questions.solution:
Let the observations be $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{20}$ and $\bar{x}$ be their mean. Given that, variance $=5$ and $n=$ 20. We know that,
Variance $\left(\sigma^2\right)=\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{20}\left(x_i-\bar{x}\right)^2$
i.e. $5=\frac{1}{20} \sum_{i=1}^{20}\left(x_i-\bar{x}\right)^2$
or $\sum_{i=1}^{20}\left(x_i-\bar{x}\right)^2=100$  .....(i)
If each observation is multiplied by 2 and the new resulting observations are $y_i$, then
$y_i=2 x_i$ i.e., $x_i=\frac{1}{2} y_i$
Therefore,
$\overline{\mathrm{y}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}} \sum_{\mathrm{i}=1}^{20} \mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{i}}=\frac{1}{20} \sum_{\mathrm{i}=1}^{20} 2 \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}=2 \cdot \frac{1}{20} \sum_{\mathrm{i}=1}^{20} \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}$
i.e., $\bar{y}=2 \bar{x}$ or $\bar{x}=\frac{1}{2} \bar{y}$.
On substituting the values of $x_i$ and $\bar{x}$ in eq. (i), we get
$\sum_{i=1}^{20}\left(\frac{1}{2} y_i-\frac{1}{2} \bar{y}\right)^2=100$
i.e., $\sum_{i=1}^{20}\left(y_i-\bar{y}\right)^2=400$
Thus, the variance of new observations
$=\frac{1}{20} \times 400=20=2^2 \times 5$.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor with plate area A and plate separation $d=2 \mathrm{~m}$ has a capacitance of $4 \mu \mathrm{~F}$. The new capacitance of the system if half of the space between them is filled with a dielectric material of dielectric constant $\mathrm{K}=3$ (as shown in figure) will be:
questions.solution: We have, $C_i=\frac{A \epsilon_0}{d}=4 \mu FC_f=\frac{A \epsilon_0}{d-t+\frac{t}{k}}=\frac{A \epsilon_0}{d-\frac{d}{2}+\frac{d}{2 \times 3}}=\frac{A \in_0}{d\left(1-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{6}\right)}=\frac{4 \mu F}{\frac{2}{3}}=6 \mu F$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Five cells each of emf $E$ and internal resistance $r$ send the same amount of current through an external resistance $R$ whether the cells are connected in parallel or in series. Then the ratio $\left(\frac{R}{r}\right)$ is
questions.solution:
Given : Number of cells, $n=5$, emf of each cell $=E$
Internal resistance of each cell $=r$
In series, current through resistance $RI=\frac{n E}{n r+R}=\frac{5 E}{5 r+R}$
In parallel, current through resistance $RI^{\prime}=\frac{E}{\frac{r}{n}+R}=\frac{n E}{r+n R}=\frac{5 E}{r+5 R}$
According to question, $I=I^{\prime}\therefore \frac{5 E}{5 r+5 R}=\frac{5 E}{r+5 R} \Rightarrow 5 r+R=r+5 R$
or $R=r \quad \therefore \frac{R}{r}=1$

questions.q: The kinetic energy of a satellite in its orbit around the earth is E . What should be the kinetic energy of the satellite so as to enable it to escape from the gravitational pull of the earth?
questions.solution:
We know that $v_e=\sqrt{2} v_0$, where $\mathrm{v}_0$ is orbital velocity.
K.E. in the orbit, $E=\frac{1}{2} M v_0{ }^2$
K.E. to escape $E=\frac{1}{2} M v_e^2=\frac{1}{2} M\left(2 v_0{ }^2\right)=\frac{1}{2} M v_0^2 \times 2=2 E$

questions.q: A simple pendulum doing small oscillations at a place R height above earth surface has time period of $T_1=4 \mathrm{~s}$. $T_2$ would be it's time period if it is brought to a point which is at a height $2 R$ from earth surface.
